skill.name: agent-tool-builder

content.value_statement: Poorly defined tools cause invalid calls, silent failures, and wasted tokens. This skill guides schema design, validation, error handling, MCP integration, and parallel execution.
actual_capabilities: Defines clear tool names, descriptions, parameters, required fields, enums, and strict schema constraints.
Adds realistic input examples for nested or format-sensitive tool arguments.
Designs structured errors that help agents identify failures and recover.
Shows MCP server patterns for listing tools, handling calls, and returning results.
Explains Anthropic and TypeScript tool runners for managed function-calling loops.
Organizes independent tool calls for parallel execution and unified result handling.
limitations: Provides design guidance and examples, but does not generate a complete production integration automatically.
Does not replace provider documentation for current SDK methods or model support.
Requires environment-specific testing for authentication, permissions, timeouts, and external service behavior.
Does not evaluate deployed tools or verify their runtime security.

use_cases.title: Define a First Agent Tool
use_cases.description: Create a clear schema, parameter descriptions, and recoverable errors for a new function-calling integration.
use_cases.target_user: Application developers adding their first AI tool

use_cases.title: Standardize an MCP Service
use_cases.description: Review tool discovery, call handling, response formatting, and access controls before sharing an MCP server.
use_cases.target_user: Platform engineers maintaining reusable agent infrastructure

use_cases.title: Improve Tool Reliability
use_cases.description: Diagnose invalid calls, ambiguous descriptions, silent failures, and inefficient sequential execution in an existing agent.
use_cases.target_user: AI product teams improving production agents

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Tool Schema
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a tool for [task]. Define its name, purpose, parameters, required fields, constraints, return text, and likely validation errors.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: creating one focused function-calling tool

prompt_templates.title: Improve an Existing Tool
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this tool definition: [definition]. Identify ambiguous descriptions, missing constraints, weak examples, and unrecoverable errors. Provide a revised design.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an MCP Server
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an MCP server for [system]. Define a small tool set, schemas, permissions, error behavior, transport, observability, and integration tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: designing a reusable multi-tool service

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Production Tool Loop
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this agent tool loop: [workflow]. Assess selection accuracy, validation, retries, timeouts, parallel calls, result ordering, access control, and test coverage.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: reviewing reliability and operational risk

output_examples.input: Design a customer lookup tool using an email address.
output_examples.output: A focused lookup design with a validated email parameter, explicit not-found behavior, permission errors, and a concise customer summary.

output_examples.input: Improve a vague weather tool that only says it gets weather.
output_examples.output: A revised description states supported locations, units, current-weather scope, expected response details, and recovery guidance for invalid places.

output_examples.input: Review four independent research tools for execution speed.
output_examples.output: The review groups independent calls for parallel execution, preserves result identifiers, combines responses once, and isolates retries for failed services.

best_practices: Describe when each tool applies, what every parameter means, and what the result contains.
Validate all model-provided inputs before execution and return errors that support recovery.
Test tool selection and argument quality with the target model alongside conventional unit and integration tests.
anti_patterns: Do not expose many overlapping tools with vague names or descriptions.
Do not return silent failures, generic errors, or unstructured implementation details.
Do not concatenate user input into SQL, shell commands, URLs, or other executable contexts.

faq.question: What types of tools does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers function-calling tools, MCP tools, schema design, validation, error handling, tool runners, and parallel execution.

faq.question: Does it implement the tool for me?
faq.answer: It guides design and implementation patterns. You still adapt the result to your SDK, services, permissions, and deployment environment.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Can it improve an existing tool schema?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the schema and expected behavior so it can identify ambiguity, missing constraints, weak errors, and testing gaps.

faq.question: Does it support MCP servers?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes MCP tool discovery, call handling, response formatting, transport setup, access controls, and interoperability guidance.

faq.question: How should generated designs be verified?
faq.answer: Run schema validation, unit tests, integration tests, model-based tool selection tests, permission checks, and failure-path tests before deployment.
